cases.analysis: Local and cloud are indistinguishable here, and the only fabrication comes from the cloud side: Haiku describes a geothermal field — steam vents, volcanic terrain — that does not exist, having decided the bamboo poles were venting. The five local models are duller and entirely honest. Paying more bought a hallucination.

cases.comment: Water monitor lizard. Forbidden list is the set of real observed confusions.

cases.analysis: The one frame where the gap is real. All five local models fail, in five directions — duck, snake, otter, snapping turtle, alligator — and two Gemmas invent an angler with tackle rather than admit uncertainty. Cloud does better but not well: Haiku says seal, and all three GPT-5.6s say turtle, the exact wrong answer the retired fixture rewarded. Only Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 name the monitor lizard. If species precision matters, no local model can currently deliver it.

cases.analysis: Nobody mistook the portholes for a ship, so the trap went unsprung and every model passes. The difference is ambition rather than accuracy: Janus offers 'depicts, modern, building', Opus works out it is a brutalist car park. For search, local is sufficient here.

cases.comment: Silhouetted crowd under a vermilion shrine frame at night, hung with BOTH paper lanterns and glass furin wind chimes (confirmed by the photographer). Either reading is correct, so both terms are accepted. A zoom of one region shows only furin - which is why a single crop is not sufficient evidence to relabel a whole frame. 'fireworks' is the only wrong answer any model gave here.

Sonnet and Fable identify glass furin wind chimes where everyone else says lanterns — both are right, the photographer confirms both are hanging, which is why one crop was never enough to relabel the frame.

cases.analysis: No fails either side, but the backlit panel exposes the depth difference. Opus reads the rig — perforated metal, circular holes, backlit bokeh — and Qwen, alone among the local models, also catches 'perforated'. Janus invents a cat bed and some sunshine. Gemma Q4 retreats to 'abstract', 'cozy', 'moment': three words nobody has ever typed into a search box.
